title: API Schema Discovery and Runtime Capability Protocol
author: Avery Kim
body:
Summary

This document defines Redwood's standard for API schema discovery and runtime capability negotiation. The protocol provides a small set of discovery endpoints, a capability advertisement model, and a client-server handshake for adaptive behavior (feature gating, streaming vs batch, partial-result checkpoints). It is intended to reduce on-call cognitive load during client rollouts, to make progressive enhancement safer across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, and to enable measurable compatibility guarantees for downstream teams.

Goals
- Provide a single, discoverable lightweight protocol for clients and intermediaries to determine: supported endpoints, supported streaming/partial-result modes, soft-deprecations, and performance advice (e.g., preferred batching window).
- Allow clients to adapt at runtime to deployed model variants and platform capabilities without hard failures.
- Make changes observable and auditable: every capability change must be surfaced in telemetry and release notes.
- Minimize coupling: discovery responses are advisory and do not change hard contract semantics except where explicitly versioned.

Scope
This standard covers:
- API discovery endpoints and semantics for Redwood services (hosted API and internal IPs used by Redwood runtime).
- Runtime capability advertisement for model-serving features (quantization support, streaming, function calling support, structured output acceptance).
- Backwards-compatible negotiation patterns used by SDKs and first-party clients.

Principles
1) Advisory-first: Discovery responses are advisory; clients should not rely on discovery for correctness but for optimization and graceful degradation.
2) Explicit versioning: Any breaking capability must be behind a major version and announced via ADR + release notes.
3) Telemetry-linked: Discovery changes produce telemetry events and optional changelog entries tied to deployment IDs.
4) Minimal surface: Keep the discovery payload small; avoid including large model manifests in the primary discovery endpoint.

Protocol overview
- Discovery endpoint: GET /.well-known/redwood-discovery (short, cacheable)
- Capabilities endpoint (detail): GET /v1/discovery/capabilities (stable, requires auth)
- Client handshake header: X-Redwood-Client-Negotiate: <client-id>/<client-version>
- Server response header: X-Redwood-Server-Capabilities-ETag: <etag> for efficient revalidation

Discovery endpoint: /.well-known/redwood-discovery
- Purpose: fast, network-cacheable summary for low-latency clients and edge proxies.
- Response semantics: 200 OK with short JSON body; cache-control max-age default 60s for hosted, configurable for dedicated/private (customer-controlled).
- Minimal fields:
  - service: short name (string)
  - api_root: base URI for the API (string)
  - capabilities_hint: list of short strings, e.g. ["streaming:v2","partial-checkpoints"]
  - supported_versions: list of strings (example: ["2026-01","2025-10"])

Example (short):
{
  "service": "redwood-text",
  "api_root": "https://api.redwood.ai/v1",
  "capabilities_hint": ["streaming:v2", "structured-output"],
  "supported_versions": ["2026-01"]
}

Capability detail endpoint: /v1/discovery/capabilities
- Purpose: machine-readable authoritative capability manifest (authenticated).
- Response: larger JSON with structured entries; still intentionally shallow (no nested objects deeper than one level). Fields to include:
  - version: semantic release tag for the manifest (string)
  - generated_at: ISO timestamp (string)
  - feature_list: list of feature tokens with optional short description strings (format: "token:short-desc")
  - compatibility_matrix_url: link to the canonical matrix doc for clients to consult
  - recommended_client_behavior: list of tokens describing best-effort client actions (e.g., "fallback-to-sync")
  - telemetry_tag: release or deployment id for correlating changes to metrics

Example capability entry (text):
{
  "version": "cap-manifest-2026-01-12",
  "generated_at": "2026-01-10T18:22:00Z",
  "feature_list": ["streaming:v2:delta-stream-encodings", "partial-checkpoints", "fncall-v1"],
  "compatibility_matrix_url": "/docs/compatibility/matrix#2026-01",
  "recommended_client_behavior": ["prefer-streaming-if-latency<200ms", "prefer-embeddings-v2-for-bulk"],
  "telemetry_tag": "deploy-2026-01-10-42"
}

Client-server negotiation flow
1) On startup (or periodically), client fetches /.well-known/redwood-discovery. If content suggests capability change (etag or capabilities_hint differs), client retrieves /v1/discovery/capabilities.
2) Client sets header X-Redwood-Client-Negotiate: <client-id>/<client-version> and optionally X-Redwood-Want-Features: <comma-separated tokens> on API calls.
3) Server may respond with HTTP 2xx and header X-Redwood-Server-Capabilities: <comma-separated tokens> indicating the accepted/active capability subset.
4) If server cannot satisfy a required feature, it returns 412 Precondition Failed with body {"error":"unsupported_feature", "missing":[...], "suggestion":"use-version:2025-10 or set header X-Redwood-Want-Features: ..."}.

Adaptive client patterns
- Soft feature gating: clients SHOULD treat capability tokens as advisory and attempt fallback modes when available. Example: if "streaming:v2" absent, fall back to chunked polling for large outputs.
- Graceful failure: prefer 4xx with structured error and suggestion over opaque 5xx when negotiation fails.
- Progressive enablement: client libraries ship with a default tolerant mode and an opt-in strict mode for customers who want hard guarantees.

Compatibility and versioning rules
- Backwards compatible additions are allowed in capability manifests and do not require ADR. Example: adding a non-breaking token "compression:snappy" is OK.
- Breaking changes to capability semantics require an ADR and a major manifest version change. Breaking changes include removing an existing capability without a fallback, changing token semantics, or changing required fields in the canonical API payloads.
- Deprecation lifecycle:
  1) Announce in manifest with token: "deprecated:<feature>:until=<YYYY-MM-DD>" and include suggestion text.
  2) Leave advisory state for >= 90 days (hosted) or customer-agreed window (Dedicated/Private).
  3) After deprecation window, remove capability with ADR and rollout plan.

Observability and telemetry
Every manifest publish or capability change must generate: 
- event.discovery.manifest.published (includes telemetry_tag, manifest version, actor)
- metric.discovery.manifest.retrieval.latency (ms)
- histogram.client.negotiation.latency (ms)
- trace spans for discovery fetches linked to request traces when negotiation affects a request
Additionally, clients SHOULD include the negotiated capability set in request traces via header X-Redwood-Client-Active-Features. This enables SLOs and impact analysis for feature rollouts.

SLOs and thresholds
- Discovery endpoint availability SLO: 99.95% (applies to hosted control plane endpoints).
- Propagation latency: 95% of golden manifests should be available via /.well-known within 2s following control plane promotion in hosted.
- Telemetry: manifest publish events must appear in ingestion within 30s for 99% of cases.
These SLOs are part of the runtime SLO budget and should be monitored by the platform metrics team.

Security considerations
- Capabilities endpoint requires authentication; do not expose detailed capability manifests on public discovery endpoints for private deployments. The short /.well-known endpoint can be used by edge proxies but must not leak customer-sensitive flags.
- All discovery payloads must be signed for private on-prem bundles (artifact signing) when used by Private deployments. Prefer HMAC with per-tenant keys or integrate with the customer's KMS for verification.

Operational playbook (short)
1) Deploy manifest to staging and verify manifest.publish event and ingestion in observability.
2) Run smoke clients against /.well-known and /v1/discovery/capabilities to validate semantics and headers.
3) Gradual rollout: hosted->canary->regional->global with telemetry gates (error rate, negotiation latency).
4) If negotiation causes user-visible failures, rollback manifest publish and revert to previous manifest version.

Testing and client guidance
- SDKs must implement a test harness that can:
  - Mock capability tokens and validate client fallbacks
  - Assert that requests include X-Redwood-Client-Negotiate and X-Redwood-Client-Active-Features headers when negotiation is used
- Integration tests: include an acceptance test that performs the full negotiation sequence and asserts no hard failures for tolerant mode.

Rollout and migration plan
- New discovery fields: ship to SDKs as optional, with one minor SDK release notifying devs of new tokens.
- Breaking capability changes: coordinate ADR, customer communications (Dedicated/Private), and 3-stage rollout with at least 90 days notice for hosted public endpoints.

Ownership and contacts
- Protocol owner: Platform API guild (triaged by API infra team). Primary contact: Avery Kim (author).
- Reviewer group: Serving Runtime, SDKs, Security. Escalation path: API infra -> Runtime -> SRE.

References and related rules
- Compatibility matrix: /docs/compatibility/matrix (internal)
- ADRs required for breaking changes: see ADR playbook in architecture-and-standards/decision-records
- Telemetry tagging conventions: observability-standards/telemetry-taxonomy

Appendix: example end-to-end sequence (concrete request/response)
1) GET https://api.redwood.ai/.well-known/redwood-discovery
Response 200: cache-control: max-age=60
{
  "service": "redwood-text",
  "api_root": "https://api.redwood.ai/v1",
  "capabilities_hint": ["streaming:v2", "partial-checkpoints"],
  "supported_versions": ["2026-01"]
}
2) Client issues POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with headers:
   X-Redwood-Client-Negotiate: sdk-js/3.4.0
   X-Redwood-Want-Features: streaming:v2,fncall-v1
3) Server responds 200 with header X-Redwood-Server-Capabilities: streaming:v2,partial-checkpoints and a streaming body encoded per streaming:v2 contract.
4) If server cannot support fncall-v1, it responds 412 with suggestion to call a rollover endpoint or use a different header set.

Questions and feedback
For questions or suggested extensions to the protocol, open an issue in the internal API infra repo and request a review by the API guild. Small, non-breaking token additions may be merged with owner sign-off; breaking semantics require an ADR.

Change log
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Avery Kim.
- 2025-12-07: Added telemetry and SLO sections after review by Observability team.
- 2026-02-03: Clarified deprecation lifecycle and added example 412 payload.
